# 1 Samuel Chapter 8 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 124v | **Source Image:** 1SA_008_page_001.jpg, 1SA_008_page_002.jpg

---

**1** And it came to pass, when Samuel was old, that he appointed his sons as judges over Israel.

**2** And the name of his firstborn son was Joel, and the name of his second, Abijah; they were judging in Beer-sheba.

**3** But his sons did not walk in his ways, and they turned aside after unjust gain and took bribes and perverted justice.

**4** Then all the elders of Israel gathered together and came to Samuel at Ramah.

**5** And they said to him, "Behold, you are old, and your sons do not walk in your ways. Now appoint for us a king to judge us like all the nations."

**6** And the matter was evil in the eyes of Samuel when they said, "Give us a king to judge us." And Samuel prayed to the LORD.

**7** And the LORD said to Samuel, "Listen to the voice of the people in all that they say to you, for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected me from reigning over them.

**8** According to all the deeds that they have done, from the day I brought them up from Egypt even to this day, in that they have forsaken me and served other gods — so they are also doing to you.

**9** Now therefore, listen to their voice; however, you shall solemnly warn them and declare to them the manner of the king who will reign over them."

**10** And Samuel spoke all the words of the LORD to the people who were asking a king from him.

**11** And he said, "This will be the manner of the king who will reign over you: your sons he will take and appoint for himself, for his chariots and for his horsemen, and they will run before his chariots.

**12** And he will appoint for himself commanders of thousands and commanders of fifties, and some to plow his plowing and to reap his harvest, and to make his implements of war and the implements of his chariots.

**13** And your daughters he will take as perfumers and as cooks and as bakers.

**14** And your fields and your vineyards and your olive groves — the best of them — he will take and give to his servants.

**15** And your seed-crops and your vineyards he will tithe, and he will give to his officers and to his servants.

**16** And your male servants and your female servants and your best young men and your donkeys he will take and put to his work.

**17** Your flocks he will tithe, and you yourselves will become his servants.

**18** And you will cry out on that day because of your king whom you have chosen for yourselves, and the LORD will not answer you on that day."

**19** But the people refused to listen to the voice of Samuel, and they said, "No! Rather, a king shall be over us,

**20** and we also shall be like all the nations, and our king will judge us and go out before us and fight our battles."

**21** And Samuel heard all the words of the people, and he spoke them in the ears of the LORD.

**22** And the LORD said to Samuel, "Listen to their voice and make a king reign over them." And Samuel said to the men of Israel, "Go, each man to his city."

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

**Verse 3** — Heb. wayyittu 'acharei habatsa' (root nata + betsa'): "turned aside after unjust gain." The noun betsa' denotes dishonest profit or plunder. The verb nata ("turned aside") marks a deliberate deviation from the path of their father.

**Verse 5** — "Like all the nations" (kekhol haggoyim): This phrase is theologically loaded. Israel's desire to conform to the governance pattern of surrounding peoples constitutes a rejection of the LORD's direct kingship (v. 7).

**Verse 7** — The LORD's response draws a sharp distinction: the people have not rejected Samuel the prophet, but the LORD himself as their sovereign. The verb ma'asu ("rejected") carries the weight of repudiation.

**Verse 11** — "The manner of the king" (mishpat hammelekh): The term mishpat here does not mean "justice" but "customary practice" or "prerogative" — what the king will claim as his right.

**Verse 16** — The MT reads "your best young men" (bachureikhem hattovim). The LXX reads "your best cattle" (boqreikhem), suggesting a possible variant reading in the Vorlage.

**Verse 18** — "The LORD will not answer you on that day": A severe prophetic warning — the very king chosen to replace divine rule will become the source of their distress, and God will withhold deliverance.

-- LOGOS
